art_direction: Award-winning Editorial / Modern Academic. High-craft, typography-driven, sophisticated. Emphasizes authority through deep navy and teal accents on a warm bone-white background. It uses generous whitespace, strict grids, and premium purposeful motion.

typography.rules: Headings must use Playfair Display with tight tracking. Body text uses Outfit for a clean, modern geometric feel. Never center-align paragraphs. Use italics selectively in headings for an editorial 'magazine' feel.

colors.rules: Avoid pure black and pure white where possible. The background should be a warm 'bone' or 'paper' color to reduce eye strain and feel like a physical journal. Accents are deep navy and teal, conveying academic trust.

visual_enhancers.borders: Use 1px solid borders with the defined border color (#D1CFC7) to create a structured, academic grid. Avoid soft, diffuse drop-shadows; prefer crisp lines.
visual_enhancers.radius: Minimal. Use rounded-none or rounded-sm for a sharp, 'printed' look.
visual_enhancers.textures: Subtle grain overlay (pointer-events-none) across the entire page to kill digital flatness and enhance the editorial feel.

layouts.hero: Kinetic typography. Split layout or dynamic overlapping grid. A massive H1 that reveals line-by-line on load. A spotlight/clipped image frame taking up a portion of the grid.
layouts.current_issue: Strict Swiss grid. A 'Bento' or multi-column layout where 'Original Articles', 'Commentary', and 'Law & Ethics' form distinct, heavily structured sections. Cards should not look like floating blobs, but structured table-like rows.
layouts.most_read: Numbered manifesto style. Massive serif numbers (e.g., 01, 02) taking up the left column, with the article title and view count spanning the right.
layouts.general: Mobile-first. Use generous padding (py-24 to py-32 for sections on desktop).

motion.hero_reveal: Framer Motion: masked line-by-line reveal for the main heading (staggered translateY from 100% to 0% with overflow-hidden on parent lines).
motion.scroll: Lenis smooth momentum scrolling is MANDATORY. It gives the site the premium 'weight'.
motion.parallax: Subtle parallax on the hero image or background abstract elements using Framer Motion useScroll.
motion.micro_interactions: Hover states on article rows should feature a subtle background color shift and an arrow icon translation (translate-x-1).

components.header: Sticky glassmorphism nav (backdrop-blur-xl bg-[#F7F5F0]/80 border-b border-black/5). Prominent pill-shaped 'Make a Submission' CTA in primary color.
components.marquee: Slow-moving editorial marquee (using react-fast-marquee) displaying the Journal At-a-Glance stats separated by bullets or small ornaments.
components.publication_fee_card: Highlighted notice card. Dark background (primary) with white text, creating a strong contrast block in the middle of the flow.
components.article_row: A clean flex or grid row. Author names in secondary color, Title in primary, page numbers in mono-font. A 'PDF' download button that is minimal (icon + text).

images.description: Modern architecture abstract, treated deliberately (spotlight, clipped frames) for the Hero section.
Dark academia library, used as a structural visual in the 'About the Journal' section.
Lab microscope representing medical research, for the Authors/Information sections.

instructions_to_main_agent: Install required dependencies: framer-motion, @studio-freight/react-lenis, react-fast-marquee, lucide-react.
Set up Tailwind configuration to include the custom fonts (Playfair Display, Outfit, JetBrains Mono) and the color palette specified.
Implement Lenis smooth scrolling at the root level of the application.
Build the Hero section with the 'masked line-by-line on-load reveal'. Wrap each line of text in an overflow-hidden span, and animate the inner text sliding up.
Create the 'Publication Fee Announcement' as a stark, high-contrast dark card (using the #0A192F color) to draw attention.
Structure the 'Current Issue' section using a rigorous grid. Avoid standard floating cards; use 1px borders to separate articles like a high-end printed index.
Build the 'Most Read' section as 'numbered manifesto chapters'. Use huge serif numbers (e.g., text-6xl or larger, light weight) alongside the article titles.
Include the slow editorial marquee using react-fast-marquee for the 'Journal At-a-Glance' stats.
Ensure all interactive elements have data-testid attributes.
DO NOT use raw transparent backgrounds on the sticky header; use backdrop-blur and a semi-transparent background.
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT: You tend to converge toward generic, 'on distribution' outputs. In frontend design, this creates what users call the 'AI slop' aesthetic. Avoid this: make creative, distinctive frontends that surprise and delight. Don't make generic centered layouts, simplistic gradients, and uniform styling. Create depth through layered design elements with z-index hierarchy. Use 2-3x more spacing than feels comfortable. Cramped designs look cheap. Add a subtle noise texture overlay to the entire app to give it an editorial, physical paper feel. Ensure typography drives the design—large, carefully tracked serif headings paired with clean, legible sans-serif body text.
